title: Stock preview: a ray that uses all its march steps is discarded, so the cut stock shows holes that change with the view

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
A user reported this in chat on 2026-11-22.

## What happens

In the simulation, the traced stock picture shows holes in the stock. Through a hole, the user sees the viewport grid behind the stock. The holes are on the faced floor, near the tool path. When the user orbits the camera, the holes change shape. Thus the cause is in the picture, not in the stock data.

The user saw this in a local build. The exact version is not known.

## Expected

The picture shows the stock as solid where the stock has material. A pixel that the march cannot resolve does not show the background as if the stock were cut through.

## Cause (from a read of `origin/main` f35202134, not built)

- `crates/ui/src/trace.wgsl` gives each ray `MAX_STEPS = 64` steps. Each step is `phi * RELAX` (0.9).
- Near a large flat face, at a low view angle, `phi` is small. The steps become small, and the ray uses all 64 steps before a hit. The ray returns status 2 (unreadable).
- `crates/ui/src/trace/composite.wgsl` (lines 47-50) discards each pixel that is not a resolved hit. The traced picture replaces the stock slot, so nothing is drawn behind the pixel. The user sees the background.
- The comment there says that a budget bail is "never painted as material". That rule is correct. But a hole also gives a wrong picture: the stock looks cut through.

## Not affected

The Deviate verdict, the post gate and the STL export do not read the traced picture. The G-code is not affected.

## Possible fixes

1. Paint a budget bail at the last march point, with a tint that shows that it is approximate. Do not discard it.
2. Increase the step budget, or set a minimum step near a surface (for example a fraction of the cell).
3. Keep the CPU twin (`camcraft_sim::stock_sim::preview::march`) in parity. The parity test is `crates/ui/tests/trace_parity.rs`.

## Related

- #3336: stock simulation performance.
- The `machined.rs` mesh is not shown when the GPU eye traces. A separate change can show the mesh when the transport is down.

Done means: a grazing view of a faced stock floor shows no background pixels inside the stock outline. A test pins this on the CPU twin, and the GPU parity test stays green.
